column4: بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا places ease after hardship; the section explicitly sets this sequence against 94:5's مَعَ, clarifying that Quranic relief can be subsequent as well as co-present.
عُسْرَةٍ ... مَيْسَرَةٍ stages a debtor in straits and commands respite until ease; it concretizes both the antonym pair and the source dictionary's act of showing ease to another.
God says He intends الْيُسْرَ and does not intend الْعُسْرَ in the fasting concession, making divine accommodation a direct form of the section's paired terms.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ makes ease a divinely prepared destination for the giver who fears God, exactly the moral path developed in the section.
فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَىٰ deliberately uses facilitation for the hard destination; it is the section's sharpest boundary against treating every facilitated path as saving ease.
وَنُيَسِّرُكَ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ addresses the Prophet with the promise that God will prepare him for the easiest way, directly matching the section's speaker and path image.
Moses asks وَيَسِّرْ لِي أَمْرِي; ease is something God makes ready inside the very commission that occasions fear and burden.
Moses asks his companion not to load his affair with عُسْرًا after forgetting his pledge, staging difficulty as an added burden in a shared task.
سَاعَةِ الْعُسْرَةِ names the concrete hour of the Tabuk expedition in which divine turning and mercy accompanied the Prophet and his followers.
يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ realizes the source dictionary's “hard day” as the day opened by the trumpet blast.
غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ continues 74:9 by denying ease specifically to the unbelievers, joining the two antonyms across adjacent ayat.
وَلَقَدْ يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ directly joins divine facilitation of the Quran to remembrance, one of the section's concluding claims.
The repeated يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ returns after the account of ʿĀd, setting an accessible reminder beside an account of severe punishment.
The same Quran-for-remembrance refrain returns after Thamud, making facilitation a repeated opening within the surah's hard warnings.
The fourth يَسَّرْنَا الْقُرْآنَ لِلذِّكْرِ repeats the promise after Lot's people and confirms that this ease is meant to produce remembrance.
فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ locates the Quran's ease on the Prophet's tongue so that it can give good news and warning.
فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَاهُ بِلِسَانِكَ repeats the tongue image and states remembrance as its purpose, a direct unquoted counterpart to 19:97.
فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ makes the practicable portion of Quran the measure after God acknowledges illness, travel, fighting, and inability to keep the earlier night measure.
وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَل لَّهُ مِنْ أَمْرِهِ يُسْرًا makes ease in one's affair a divine gift tied to caution, closely joining 92:5-7 and 65:7.
ثُمَّ السَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُ explicitly stages ease as a way God makes traversable for the human being.
هَذَا يَوْمٌ عَسِرٌ is the unbelievers' own recognition as they rush from the graves toward the caller, another exact Quranic “hard day.”
The day when true sovereignty belongs to the Merciful is عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ عَسِيرًا, locating hardness in the hearer's relation to judgment.
وَإِن تَعَاسَرْتُمْ names reciprocal difficulty over nursing arrangements, while the verse requires housing, support, payment, and consultation—the social opposite of making matters easy for another.
قَوْلًا مَيْسُورًا requires an accessible, gentle word when one cannot yet give to needy relatives and travelers, concretizing the dictionary sense “show ease to him.”
سَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا promises the righteous subject of Dhu al-Qarnayn an easy or gentle command, pairing just rule with ease toward another.
فَالْجَارِيَاتِ يُسْرًا pictures effortless, smoothly prepared motion; it gives a physical Quranic instance of the source gloss “made smooth and ready.”
فَسَوْفَ يُحَاسَبُ حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا makes ease the quality of the believer's reckoning, an eschatological counterpart to the hard day.
The youths ask هَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا; هَيِّئْ is the very “prepare” wording used in the source dictionary to explain how ease comes about amid their danger.
وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُم مِّنْ أَمْرِكُم مِّرْفَقًا answers the cave scene with prepared relief, making a place of refuge and facility available inside persecution.
رَبِّ اشْرَحْ لِي صَدْرِي immediately precedes Moses' request for ease in 20:26 and joins opened breast to an eased task exactly as the section joins 94:1 to 94:5.
وَاحْلُلْ عُقْدَةً مِّن لِّسَانِي turns the source dictionary's tangled, knotted difficulty into a literal knot whose loosening prepares speech.
يَفْقَهُوا قَوْلِي states what the loosening in 20:27 makes possible: an eased tongue becomes intelligible speech.
وَأَشْرِكْهُ فِي أَمْرِي asks that Aaron share Moses' task, a narrative counterpart to the section's two hands working together in one labor.
كَيْ نُسَبِّحَكَ كَثِيرًا gives the purpose of the eased and shared task: abundant glorification.
وَنَذْكُرَكَ كَثِيرًا completes the purpose of Moses' requested ease with abundant remembrance, linking eased work and dhikr.

فَقُولَا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَّيِّنًا commands Moses and Aaron to use gentle speech toward Pharaoh; this is a concrete enactment of making interaction easy for the other, and its hoped-for result is remembrance or fear.
فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَاتَّقَىٰ supplies giving and caution as the human acts to which 92:7's prepared easy path responds.
وَصَدَّقَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ adds affirmation of the best promise as the second condition completed by the ease of 92:7.
بَخِلَ وَاسْتَغْنَىٰ identifies withholding and imagined self-sufficiency as the posture that issues in 92:10's hard destination.
وَكَذَّبَ بِالْحُسْنَىٰ completes the reversal of 92:6 and explains why “facilitation” in 92:10 leads toward hardship.
سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰ promises that God will make the Prophet receive and retain recitation just before promising to prepare him for ease in 87:8.
The sick and traveler may complete the fast on other days and a feeding substitute is named; these concrete accommodations are the basis for 2:185's declaration that God intends ease.

In the same nursing scene as 65:6, no mother or father may be harmed through the child, support follows recognized means, and weaning is by mutual consultation; it shows ease practiced between people.
يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ أَن يُخَفِّفَ عَنكُمْ states God's will to lighten the human burden because the human being was created weak, a nonlexical formulation of intended ease.
After ablution and its dry substitute, مَا يُرِيدُ اللَّهُ لِيَجْعَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنْ حَرَجٍ denies that the law aims to impose constriction and instead names purification and completed favor.
وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ makes absence of religious constriction a general divine act and pairs it with holding fast to God as protector.
لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا gives capacity as the boundary of burden and ends with prayers not to be loaded beyond strength.
The Messenger يَضَعُ عَنْهُمْ إِصْرَهُمْ وَالْأَغْلَالَ removes burdens and shackles; it is a communal parallel to the load taken from the Prophet before 94:5.
مَا أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ لِتَشْقَىٰ denies that revelation was sent to make the Prophet wretched, setting a clear boundary around the section's Quran-made-easy claim.
إِلَّا تَذْكِرَةً لِّمَن يَخْشَىٰ supplies remembrance for the one who fears as revelation's purpose, joining the remembrance formulas of 54 with the fearing recipient of 87 and 92.
إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا calls revelation a heavy word, while 73:20 makes its recited amount easy; the same Quran can be weighty in charge and accommodated in practice.
قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ presents the Quran as free of crookedness so that people may fear God, the precise nonlexical reverse of difficulty defined as bending and entanglement.
وَتَحْسَبُونَهُ هَيِّنًا وَهُوَ عِندَ اللَّهِ عَظِيمٌ makes “light/trivial” the speakers' false estimate of slander; it sharply limits the dictionary equation of easy with insignificant.
هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ uses هَيِّن, the source dictionary's gloss for يَسِير, for God's creation of John despite humanly impossible conditions.
هُوَ عَلَيَّ هَيِّنٌ repeats the same dictionary synonym in Mary's harder-seeming case and grounds ease in divine power rather than ordinary conditions.
God says He sent down a book فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ; revelation itself carries the addressees' remembrance or honor, joining the section's raised name to the Quran made easy for dhikr.
وَإِنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ makes the Quran a remembrance or honor for the Prophet and his people, directly bridging elevated mention and facilitated revelation.
After 9:117's hour of hardship, the earth becomes narrow despite its vastness and the three men's souls constrict before God turns to them, showing inner and outer constriction opening into mercy.
In the cave, the Prophet says لَا تَحْزَنْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَنَا before tranquility and unseen aid descend; divine ease is present “with” danger rather than waiting for danger to vanish.
God answers Moses and Aaron's fear with إِنَّنِي مَعَكُمَا أَسْمَعُ وَأَرَىٰ, placing divine accompaniment inside the feared mission for which Moses requested ease.
When the two groups see each other at the sea, Moses says إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ; guidance is asserted within apparent entrapment before the path opens.
After believers are shaken until the messenger asks when help will come, أَلَا إِنَّ نَصْرَ اللَّهِ قَرِيبٌ places relief at the extremity of hardship.
Jacob commands his sons to search and not despair مِن رَّوْحِ اللَّهِ; expected divine relief remains available while Joseph and his brother are still absent.
When messengers reach the point of despair and think themselves denied, جَاءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا; it stages help at the tightest point of difficulty.
God expands the breast of the guided but makes the breast of the one led astray ضَيِّقًا حَرَجًا, a bodily contrast that illuminates opened breast as ease within the section.
An opened breast receiving light is set against hearts hardened from God's remembrance; this binds expansion, hardness, and dhikr in one explicit contrast.
أَيَّامٍ نَّحِسَاتٍ calls the wind-punishment days ill-omened, giving a Quranic scene for the source dictionary's secondary “unlucky day” sense of difficulty.
فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُّسْتَمِرٍّ names the day of ʿĀd's violent wind an enduring day of ill omen, another direct scene for that dictionary sense.
ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا describes the shadow's easy or gentle withdrawal, a physical instance of ease as a light, smoothly executed action.
Calamity is written before it occurs and إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ; human hardship and divine ease occupy the same event from different standpoints.
Casting the aggressive wrongdoer into fire is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا; “easy for God” plainly does not mean slight in consequence.
Everlasting passage into hell is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا, again separating divine ease of enactment from moral or experiential lightness.
God's complete knowledge and prior record of heaven and earth are إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, locating ease in divine mastery over an immense matter.
The origination and repetition of creation are إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, showing that what appears resistant to creatures is ready for God.
The cancellation of the fearful hypocrites' deeds is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا, using the root for decisive divine action rather than a pleasant human experience.
A doubled punishment is وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرًا; the verse directly blocks “easy” from being heard as small or lenient punishment.
Every lengthened or shortened life is in a record and إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, presenting exhaustive measure as easy for God.
The earth splitting as people emerge swiftly for gathering is حَشْرٌ عَلَيْنَا يَسِيرٌ, an easy divine gathering on the very day other ayat call hard for unbelievers.
After deniers reject resurrection, God says raising and informing them of their deeds is وَذَٰلِكَ عَلَى اللَّهِ يَسِيرٌ, opposing perceived impossibility with divine ease.
وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰ shows that the self-sufficiency of 92:8 cannot rescue its owner when the hard path reaches its fall.
إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا لَلْهُدَىٰ places guidance under divine care immediately after the paired easy and hard destinations, reinforcing that these are paths, not mere moods.
فَذَكِّرْ إِن نَّفَعَتِ الذِّكْرَىٰ turns the preparation for ease in 87:8 into the Prophet's work of reminding.
سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ identifies the fearing person as the one who receives that reminder, paralleling the cautious giver prepared for ease in 92.
قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا sets the demanding night practice in a limited quantity; 73:20 later translates that measured burden into “what is easy” of Quran.
نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ انقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا makes the amount adjustable downward, a concrete link to the section's secondary sense of يَسِير as little.
أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ allows a measured increase and commands deliberate recitation, completing the adjustable practice later eased in 73:20.
وَاجْعَل لِّي وَزِيرًا مِّنْ أَهْلِي asks for a helper as part of Moses' answer to a difficult commission; the helper will make the single task shared.
هَارُونَ أَخِي identifies the companion who will supply the second worker in the shared labor developed through 20:32.
اشْدُدْ بِهِ أَزْرِي asks that Aaron strengthen Moses' back, reversing the load that breaks the back in the surrounding surah 94 image.
اذْهَبَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ sends the two together into the feared task, the setting in which 20:44 requires gentleness and 20:46 promises divine company.
فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ supplies the trumpet event that makes 74:9's “hard day” a concrete eschatological scene.
People emerge from the graves with humbled eyes like scattered locusts; this supplies the bodily scene whose unbelieving speech in 54:8 calls the day hard.
The sky splits with cloud and angels descend, furnishing the event that 25:26 calls a hard day for unbelievers.
Receiving the record in the right hand is the concrete event whose consequence 84:8 names an easy account.
Receiving the record behind the back begins the opposite branch from 84:7-8's easy account, so the ease is shown as a discriminating outcome rather than a universal one.
The Prophet's gentleness keeps people near, while harshness and hard-heartedness would scatter them; pardon and consultation enact the source dictionary's ease toward another.
قَصْدُ السَّبِيلِ is set against paths that are جَائِرٌ; directed and deviating ways provide a Quranic path image for ease as straight readiness versus difficulty as bending away.
God's straight path is singular while the other ways split people away from it, an explicit path boundary for the section's one prepared way and resistant deviation.
The Book is sent down with no عِوَجًا; its absence of crookedness directly joins revelation to the source's contrast between tangled resistance and prepared ease.
قَيِّمًا continues 18:1 by presenting the Book as upright so that it can warn and give believers good news, the operative consequence of its uncrooked form.
The Quran guides لِلَّتِي هِيَ أَقْوَمُ, joining the eased revelation to the most upright course it opens for its hearers.
Believers are told to seek help through patience and prayer because إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ; divine company is located within endurance of difficulty.
Dispute would make the believers falter and lose strength, while patience carries the promise إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ; entangling opposition and sustaining company are placed side by side.
The righteous fear يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا, a nonlexical depiction of the grim hard day that the section traces through عَسِير.
Those who love the immediate life leave behind them يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا; the “heavy day” is a nonlexical counterimage to the source's easy as light.
مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ reassures the same Prophet that present silence does not mean abandonment, a stance of consolation continuous with 94's promise in difficulty.
وَلَلْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ لَّكَ مِنَ الْأُولَىٰ promises a better later condition; its temporal sequence complements and contrasts with 94:5's simultaneous مَعَ.
وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ promises future giving and satisfaction to the same addressee, another form of divinely prepared relief.
أَلَمْ يَجِدْكَ يَتِيمًا فَآوَىٰ recalls shelter within the Prophet's earlier vulnerability, like 94:1-4's past favors serving as evidence for promised ease.
وَوَجَدَكَ ضَالًّا فَهَدَىٰ recalls guidance out of being without a way, supporting the section's image of ease as an opened path.
وَوَجَدَكَ عَائِلًا فَأَغْنَىٰ recalls sufficiency following need, another past divine act grounding reassurance to the Prophet.
فَلَا اقْتَحَمَ الْعَقَبَةَ calls the morally saving way a steep ascent; it limits any reading of 92's prepared easy way as requiring no strenuous act.
فَكُّ رَقَبَةٍ defines the steep ascent through freeing a person, a costly giving act that nonetheless aligns with the giver led to ease in 92.
إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ places feeding inside a day of hunger, a precise scene of beneficial action and hardship occurring together.
The orphan of kin is one recipient of that feeding, specifying the generosity that belongs to the difficult ascent and the path of ease.
أَوْ مِسْكِينًا ذَا مَتْرَبَةٍ adds the destitute person in dust, keeping the act of ease toward another inside severe need.
Mutual counsel to patience and mercy completes the steep path; endurance and mercy explain how moral ease coexists with exertion.
Every messenger is sent in his people's language لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ; intelligible language supplies the communicative purpose behind the Quran being eased on the Prophet's tongue.
The imagined non-Arabic Quran prompts an objection about its signs and language, while the actual revelation is guidance and healing; it clarifies why ease on the Prophet's tongue matters to hearers.
خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ gives a Quranic dual-hand expression directed to one act; it may echo the source's two hands at one work, though the ayah itself does not speak of ease or hardship.

بَلْ يَدَاهُ مَبْسُوطَتَانِ joins the dual-hand image to unrestricted giving; it may illuminate the source's two hands working together, though its main contrast is with the false claim of a fettered divine hand.
Whoever fears God receives مَخْرَجًا, a way out; this opens the same passage as 65:4 and 65:7 and makes ease a path emerging from constriction.
God provides from where the person could not reckon and is sufficient for one who trusts Him, specifying the hidden provision that accompanies 65:2's exit and 65:4's ease.
Job names the harm that has touched him while addressing the Most Merciful, giving a concrete afflicted speaker whose difficulty remains present in the prayer.
God answers Job, removes his harm, and gives back his family with as many again; one affliction is answered by doubled gift, a close thematic counterpart to one hardship and more than one ease.
Jonah calls from layered darkness that there is no god but God and that he has wronged himself, staging remembrance from inside distress rather than after it.
God answers Jonah and saves him from anguish, then says He likewise saves believers; the ayah turns one rescue into a continuing promise of relief.
Job says that suffering and torment have touched him, introducing the resistant bodily hardship answered immediately in the next ayah.
Job is told to strike with his foot and finds a cool washing place and drink; the commanded movement opens bodily ease inside the affliction of 38:41.
God restores Job's family and as many with them as mercy and reminder, again placing a doubled gift after one named suffering.
God answers Noah's earlier call and saves him and his household from the great anguish, a concise direct formulation of relief from constriction.
God saves Noah and his household مِنَ الْكَرْبِ الْعَظِيمِ, giving the hardship-to-rescue half of a passage that then raises his mention.
God leaves something for Noah among later generations; 37:79 supplies its content, so this ayah contributes the enduring raised-mention act after rescue.
سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ نُوحٍ فِي الْعَالَمِينَ states the lasting honorable mention left after Noah's rescue in 37:76, directly joining removed distress and elevated name.
God saves Moses, Aaron, and their people from the great anguish, another exact rescue formulation concerning the same Moses who asks for ease elsewhere.
God leaves something for Moses and Aaron among later generations; 37:120 names that lasting mention, following their rescue from great anguish.
سَلَامٌ عَلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ gives Moses and Aaron an enduring honorable mention after 37:115's deliverance, again binding relief and raised remembrance.
A day that makes children gray is set before the same surah's accommodated Quran reading in 73:20; the passage holds an unbearably hard day beside a practicable present duty.
Patience and prayer are commanded as means of help, yet prayer is called difficult except for the humble; a divinely given means of ease can itself feel heavy to its practitioner.
The regulated remission in retaliation is called a lightening from the Lord and mercy, a concrete legal reduction of burden parallel to the fasting concession.
In regulating care for orphans, the ayah says that had God willed He could have made matters difficult for the believers; the unrealized hardship clarifies divine accommodation in social law.
Amid commands about orphan property, measure, and truthful speech, God says He charges no soul beyond its capacity, extending the section's burden-and-ease relation into daily justice.
The righteous are promised the garden with the reminder that God charges no soul beyond its capacity, joining bounded burden to the easy outcome of salvation.
God charges no soul beyond its capacity and has a truthful record, presenting measured obligation as a standing divine rule rather than a single concession.
Believers are told to fear God as much as they are able, listen, obey, and spend; capacity directly measures the moral demand while giving remains the path's positive act.
The blind, lame, and sick bear no blame for exemption from fighting, a concrete bodily-capacity application of divine ease in obligation.

The hypocrites would have followed for nearby gain and a moderate journey, but the arduous distance deterred them; it exposes attraction to what is merely easy while refusing a difficult faithful task.
Re-creating creatures is described as easier for God, another Quranic use that grounds apparent impossibility in divine power rather than calling the result insignificant.
The Prophet is told not to move his tongue hurriedly with the revelation, directly supplying the tongue and human strain presupposed by the claim that the Quran is eased on his tongue.
God assumes responsibility for collecting the revelation and its recitation, identifying the divine action that makes the Prophet's reception possible.
When God has recited it, the Prophet is told to follow its recitation; his task is made a responsive path rather than anxious self-production.
God also assumes responsibility for explaining the revelation, completing the sequence of divine collection, recitation, and clarification behind its facilitated delivery.
The revelation comes in a clear Arabic tongue; the ayah supplies the intelligible linguistic form through which being eased on the Prophet's tongue reaches hearers.
Against the charge that a human teaches the Prophet, the ayah contrasts a foreign tongue with this clear Arabic tongue, clarifying the public intelligibility involved in linguistic ease.
God grants Abraham and his family mercy and makes for them a lofty truthful mention, a direct parallel to divine relief accompanied by raised remembrance.
Abraham asks for a truthful mention among later generations, supplying the prayer-side counterpart to God's act of raising a servant's name.
Those who strive for God are promised guidance into His paths, and God is with those who do good; exertion, an opened way, and divine company occur in one formulation.
God makes the earth manageable and commands people to walk its paths and eat His provision, a physical instance of terrain made fit and ready for movement.
God makes the earth an expanse for people, supplying the prepared ground whose purpose is stated as path-travel in 71:20.
The prepared earth lets people travel broad ways, a concrete nonlexical parallel to ease staged as an opened, traversable path.
The most wretched person avoids the reminder, reversing 87:10's fearful hearer and showing the rejected side of the remembrance joined to ease in 87:8.
In battle the believers seek rescue and God answers with promised angelic reinforcement, placing responsive aid inside the moment of military distress.
The reinforcement is made good news so that hearts may become tranquil, while victory belongs only to God; inner ease arrives before the danger has ended.
Drowsiness gives security and rain purifies, removes Satan's defilement, strengthens hearts, and firms feet, a cluster of simultaneous eases within the battlefield's hardship.
God reminds the believers that He helped them at Badr while they were weak, an explicit statement of aid present within acknowledged vulnerability.
